metadata.name: Vitamin B12 deficiency
metadata.emergency_level: Routine - but neurological involvement needs prompt treatment to avoid permanent damage
metadata.severity: From mild/asymptomatic to macrocytic anaemia and serious neurological disease

overview.short_description: Deficiency of vitamin B12 (cobalamin) causing macrocytic anaemia and, importantly, neurological problems (neuropathy, cognitive change, subacute combined degeneration) that can become permanent if untreated.
overview.detailed_description: B12 deficiency is common, especially in older adults, vegans, and with malabsorption. The key clinical points are that neurological damage can occur (and may precede or occur without anaemia) and can be irreversible if treatment is delayed, and that pernicious anaemia (autoimmune loss of intrinsic factor) is a common cause. Treatment is B12 replacement, usually intramuscular, especially with neurological features.
overview.pathophysiology: B12 is a cofactor for DNA synthesis (hence megaloblastic anaemia) and myelin metabolism (hence neuropathy/subacute combined degeneration of the cord). Absorption requires intrinsic factor (from gastric parietal cells) and an intact terminal ileum.
overview.etiology: Malabsorption - pernicious anaemia (autoimmune), gastric/ileal surgery, coeliac/Crohn's, metformin/PPIs (reduced absorption); low intake (strict vegan diet); rarely, competition (bacterial overgrowth, fish tapeworm).
overview.incubation_period: Not applicable (large hepatic stores mean deficiency develops over years).
overview.natural_history: Develops gradually; haematological changes reverse with treatment, but neurological damage may be permanent if long-standing.
overview.prognosis: Excellent for anaemia; neurological recovery depends on early treatment.

prevalence.value: Common, rising with age; higher in vegans and those with malabsorption.

incidence.value: Increases with age; pernicious anaemia more common in older adults with autoimmune background.

mortality.value: Low with treatment; morbidity from untreated neurological disease.

epidemiology.sex_predominance: Pernicious anaemia slightly more common in women.

risk_factors.pregnancy: Increased demand; deficiency affects the infant.
risk_factors.genetic_factors: Autoimmune predisposition; rare inherited transport defects.
risk_factors.previous_diseases: Autoimmune conditions, gastric/ileal surgery, coeliac/Crohn's disease.

negative_findings.why_important: Reduces likelihood of deficiency (borderline levels may need active-B12/MMA if symptoms persist)
Less concern for irreversible neurological damage (but anaemia still needs treatment)

history_questions.question: Any numbness/tingling, unsteadiness, or memory changes?
history_questions.why_ask: Neurological involvement needs prompt IM treatment

history_questions.question: Diet (vegan/vegetarian) and any gastric/bowel surgery or coeliac/Crohn's?

physical_examination.examination: Neurological exam (peripheral sensation, proprioception, gait, reflexes, cognition)
physical_examination.expected_finding: Sensory neuropathy, impaired proprioception/vibration, ataxia in SCDC

vital_signs.heart_rate: May be raised if significant anaemia

laboratory_tests.expected_result: Macrocytosis (raised MCV), anaemia; hypersegmented neutrophils on film
laboratory_tests.rule_out: Normal indices do not exclude neurological B12 deficiency

laboratory_tests.test_name: Serum B12 (+/- active B12/holotranscobalamin, methylmalonic acid, folate)
laboratory_tests.expected_result: Low B12; raised MMA/homocysteine support tissue deficiency
laboratory_tests.rule_in: Low B12 (or borderline with raised MMA)

laboratory_tests.test_name: Intrinsic factor antibodies (+/- gastric parietal cell antibodies)
laboratory_tests.expected_result: Positive IF antibodies (specific) in pernicious anaemia

ecg.when_needed: If severe anaemia with cardiac symptoms

other_diagnostic_tests.endoscopy: Gastroscopy if gastric pathology suspected (pernicious anaemia associates with gastric atrophy/cancer risk)

diagnostic_criteria.formal_criteria: Low serum B12 (or borderline B12 with clinical features and raised methylmalonic acid/homocysteine). Establish the cause; test for intrinsic factor antibodies to diagnose pernicious anaemia. Treat neurological presentations promptly even before all results return.
diagnostic_criteria.cutoff_values: Thresholds are laboratory-specific; borderline results are interpreted with active-B12/MMA and clinical context (BSH).

differential_diagnosis.differences: Low folate; no neurological features from folate deficiency itself (and giving folate alone in B12 deficiency can worsen neurology)
differential_diagnosis.red_flags: Do not treat with folate alone if B12 low
differential_diagnosis.differential_questions: Is folate low with normal B12?

differential_diagnosis.disease: Other macrocytosis (alcohol, hypothyroidism, liver disease, myelodysplasia, drugs)
differential_diagnosis.distinguishing_labs: Normal B12/folate; TFTs/LFTs; marrow if needed
differential_diagnosis.differential_questions: Any alcohol, thyroid or liver disease?
Is there diabetes or another neuropathy cause with normal B12?

diagnostic_questions.question: Do you have numbness/tingling, unsteadiness, or memory change (neurological features)?
diagnostic_questions.purpose: Neurological features mandate prompt IM treatment to prevent permanent damage
diagnostic_questions.interpretation: Neurological features -> treat promptly (IM), do not delay

diagnostic_questions.question: Is folate also low? (Important - do not treat with folate alone if B12 is low.)
diagnostic_questions.interpretation: If both low, replace B12 first/alongside folate

next_best_question.question: Are there neurological features, what is the cause (diet/malabsorption/drugs), and is folate low?
next_best_question.expected_answers: Neuro vs not; cause; folate status
next_best_question.branching_logic: Neurological or pernicious anaemia -> IM B12; dietary -> oral/IM as appropriate; replace B12 before/with folate if both low; investigate cause

next_best_test.test: Serum B12 (+ MMA/active B12 if borderline) and folate
next_best_test.why: Confirms deficiency and avoids folate-alone error

red_flags.finding: Neurological features (neuropathy, ataxia, cognitive change) with low B12
red_flags.immediate_action: Treat promptly with intramuscular B12 to prevent irreversible damage
Replace B12 first/together - do NOT give folate alone (can worsen neurology)

red_flags.finding: Pernicious anaemia (gastric atrophy - increased gastric cancer risk)
red_flags.immediate_action: Lifelong treatment and awareness of GI symptoms

referral_criteria.urgent_referral: Significant neurological involvement; severe anaemia; diagnostic uncertainty.
referral_criteria.routine_referral: Refractory/unclear cause; suspected malabsorption; haematology input.

late: Subacute combined degeneration of the cord (may be permanent)

initial_management.supportive_care: Explain the cause and treatment; note lifelong treatment for pernicious anaemia/irreversible malabsorption.
initial_management.medications: Canonical schema 1.3 guidance: use treatment_guidance.medication_options and its history-based safety checks. Candidate classes/options (not a prescription): Oral vitamin B12; Intramuscular vitamin B12. No autonomous selection or dosing is allowed. Source IDs: NICE_NG239.
initial_management.lifestyle_advice: Dietary B12 (animal products; fortified foods/supplements for vegans); review causative drugs.
initial_management.follow_up: Monitor haematological response; ongoing replacement per cause; monitor neurological recovery.
initial_management.legacy_medications_pre_v13: Intramuscular hydroxocobalamin (loading then maintenance) - especially with neurological features or pernicious anaemia; oral B12 (higher dose) may suffice for dietary deficiency or maintenance in some. If both B12 and folate are low, treat B12 first/together, then folate. Address the underlying cause.

patient_education.home_advice: Vitamin B12 is needed for blood and nerves. Low levels cause tiredness and, importantly, nerve symptoms like numbness, pins-and-needles or unsteadiness that must be treated promptly to avoid lasting damage. Treatment is usually B12 injections (sometimes tablets). If the cause is your body not absorbing B12 (pernicious anaemia or after surgery), treatment is lifelong. Vegans should take a B12 supplement.
patient_education.home_advice_ar: فيتامين B12 ضروري للدم والأعصاب. نقصه يسبّب التعب، والأهم أعراضاً عصبية كالتنميل والوخز وعدم الاتزان يجب علاجها بسرعة لتجنّب ضرر دائم. العلاج غالباً حقن B12 (وأحياناً أقراص). إن كان السبب عدم امتصاص الجسم للفيتامين (فقر الدم الوبيل أو بعد جراحة) فالعلاج مدى الحياة. على النباتيين الصرفين تناول مكمّل B12.
patient_education.prevention: B12 supplementation for vegans and at-risk groups; monitor with long-term metformin/PPI use.
patient_education.warning_signs: New numbness/tingling, unsteadiness, weakness, or memory/mood change - seek prompt review.

prevention.lifestyle: Adequate dietary B12; supplementation for vegans/at-risk.
prevention.screening: Consider testing in at-risk groups (vegans, malabsorption, long-term metformin/PPI, older adults with suggestive symptoms).

evidence.evidence_level: High for B12 replacement; strong emphasis on prompt treatment of neurological deficiency.
evidence.guideline_strength: The main diagnosis/test and treatment direction was checked against the current guidance identified by NICE_NG239; see evidence_review for scope and limitations. This does not verify every legacy narrative sentence.
evidence.legacy_guideline_strength_pre_v13: Strong - BSH (British Society for Haematology), NICE CKS.
